# RETRO: PR #13106

## What worked
- Neutral brief naming the Codex CLI source as in scope: both reviewers independently pinned the same tag (rust-v0.156.1) and reached the same findings, so no cross-examination follow-ups were needed.
- Opus built stub replies from upstream source, which made base/head runtime comparisons meaningful. Coordinator spot-checked the four key upstream line ranges before drafting.

## Friction and deviations
- Opus subagent could not write its report file ("Subagents should return findings as text"). The coordinator saved the SubagentHandback message verbatim from the transcript to opus/final-report.md (sha256 0f0d831e...). First extraction attempt grabbed the wrong text block; it is preserved as opus/closing-summary.md. Suggested fix: the omarchy-reviewer definition or brief should say the final report is delivered via handback, or the tooling should allow the write.
- Read-size bound: Opus reported eight parallel 50-line reads (about 400 lines in one turn), three single responses of 51-66 lines, and a `cut -c` projection used only to locate write targets. Sol reported two reads of 100 and 85 lines. Disclosed; no effect on host state; source claims were independently confirmed.
- Opus did not read test lines 101-599 line by line (covered by greps and runs).
- Coordinator: first author_policy call passed a URL string instead of a PR dict (crash, no decision); rerun with fetched identity passed. A `sleep 45 && poll` was blocked by the harness; polled directly instead.
- No markdown renderer on host; wrote a small assignment-local render_html.py.

## Carry forward
- Tell the Opus reviewer its final report arrives as handback text.
- Repeat the one-read-per-turn guidance more forcefully for parallel calls.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** With Codex's default file credential store, a missing `$CODEX_HOME/auth.json` means no login, and the collector now returns before starting `codex app-server`. Local Codex, pi, omp and opencode usage stats are still reported. For these users the skipped probe loses nothing: `account/rateLimits/read` can only return an authentication error. The new test assertion fails on the base collector and passes on this head.

The credential check also has false negatives (logged-in users treated as logged out) and false positives (variables that do not log in the app-server), described below.

### Logged-in users without `auth.json` lose their rate limits

The check at [`bin/omarchy-agent-usage-codex:529-536`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/bfbba36833173e6db923717e7181f02820d51805/bin/omarchy-agent-usage-codex#L529-L536) treats "no `auth.json` and no API-key variable" as "not logged in". At Codex `rust-v0.156.1`, two supported login paths leave no `auth.json`:

- `cli_auth_credentials_store = "keyring"` or `"auto"` in `config.toml`. Saving credentials to the keyring deletes `auth.json` ([`login/src/auth/storage.rs#L300-L310`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.156.1/codex-rs/login/src/auth/storage.rs#L300-L310)).
- A `CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN` login, which Codex reads before its persistent store and which uses the Codex backend, so rate limits are readable.

Collector output with a stub `codex` that answers as a logged-in app-server (synthetic, `--limits-only`):

| Case | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `auth.json` present | 2 limits, plan shown | 2 limits, plan shown |
| no `auth.json` (keyring/auto store) | 2 limits, plan shown | no limits, "Codex limits unavailable" |
| no `auth.json`, `CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN` set | 2 limits, plan shown | no limits, "Codex limits unavailable" |

**Impact:** These users lose their 5-hour and weekly meters and are told to run `codex login`. In keyring mode that does not help, because a new login again saves to the keyring and deletes `auth.json`. The file store is the default, so most users are unaffected.

**Suggested change:** Apply the `auth.json` shortcut only when the configured store is `file` (read `cli_auth_credentials_store` from `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml`, for example with `tomllib`, and fall through to the probe for `keyring`/`auto`). Treat a non-empty `CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN` as a possible login.

### `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `CODEX_API_KEY` do not log in `codex app-server`

At `rust-v0.156.1` the app-server builds its auth manager with the environment API key disabled ([`app-server/src/lib.rs#L805-L808`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.156.1/codex-rs/app-server/src/lib.rs#L805-L808)), and login resolution never reads `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Rate limits also need a Codex-backend login: an API key gets "chatgpt authentication required to read rate limits" ([`account_processor.rs#L1107-L1121`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.156.1/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/account_processor.rs#L1107-L1121)).

```text
no auth.json + OPENAI_API_KEY or CODEX_API_KEY exported
  -> check passes, app-server starts on every refresh
  -> no Codex login, so no remote plugin catalog
  -> curated plugin repo sync runs (the reported side effect)
  -> rateLimits/read fails, no limits shown
```

**Impact:** Users with no Codex login who export either variable in the desktop session keep the plugin-repository contact the PR aims to remove, with nothing gained. This matches base behavior, so it is not a regression, but it narrows the fix for a common developer setup.

**Suggested change:** Drop the `CODEX_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY` exceptions (and add `CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN` as above).

**Optional test improvement:** The new no-credentials case inherits `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `CODEX_API_KEY` from the caller. With either variable set, the test fails falsely ("Codex collector does not spawn app-server without credentials"). Prefixing the call with `env -u OPENAI_API_KEY -u CODEX_API_KEY` made it pass in the same environment.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the pinned head and base, and of Codex CLI source at tag `rust-v0.156.1` (the PR does not state which Codex version was tested; other versions may differ). Sandboxed runs with no network: the scanner test on base and head, and direct collector runs against a stub `codex` whose replies follow the `rust-v0.156.1` source. Not tested: a live Codex binary, a real keyring or login, or a network audit.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
